subject: Finalizing arrival slots & backup legs for Globex exec workshop
messages:
From: Kate Ellis <kate.ellis@globex.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: TravelOps <travel@globex.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Jun 2027 14:03:00 -0700
Subject: Exec workshop — arrival windows and contingency legs

Ben,

Thanks again for lining up the workshop on June 24–25. Quick ask from our side: we have eight execs arriving in two clusters and procurement wants a clear allocation of arrival slots plus contingency legs if flights are delayed. Can you confirm what buffer windows Redwood can support for arrivals (i.e., preferred window, latest acceptable arrival) and any internal fallback you want us to plan to use (alternate airports, shuttle contingencies)?

Attached is our preliminary attendee schedule — you'll notice three VPs arrive earlier and five senior directors on the 24th. Procurement would like a short MUTUAL ACTION PLAN row for travel so they can reconcile invoices against arrival time.

Also: a couple of execs asked about upgrade options and whether group PNRs can be shared with our TravelOps team.

Appreciate a clear plan so we can finalize ticketing by EOD Friday.

Best,
Kate Ellis
Head of Executive Programs
Globex Corporation
Attachment: globex_attendee_list.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Kate Ellis <kate.ellis@globex.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 11 Jun 2027 09:41:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Exec workshop — arrival windows and contingency legs

Kate — thanks for the clear ask. High level below; I'll follow with an internal note on seat assignments and fallback legs.

- Preferred arrival window: 08:30–12:30 on Thu 24 Jun (we have transport and morning prep scheduled).
- Latest acceptable arrival: 16:30 on Thu 24 Jun (beyond that, we risk missing the afternoon prep and tabletop run).
- Buffer policy: we can hold two contingency shuttle slots (30 seats total) and one quick-turn hire car for same-day arrivals.
- Alternate airport: San Jose (SJC) as secondary; we can run the same shuttle plan but add a 35–45 minute transfer buffer.

I'll upload a preliminary schedule and seat matrix for your TravelOps. For the PNRs: we can share group-level PNR summaries (names redacted per privacy) with TravelOps and provide a secure link to the full PNRs for procurement sign-off.

Next steps: I'll circulate the seat matrix and a canary-legs CSV (to be used if primary flights are cancelled). Can you confirm the names that must have guaranteed window arrival vs those who are flexible? Procurement's MUTUAL ACTION PLAN row would also be helpful.

Cheers,
Ben
Principal Solutions Manager | Redwood Inference
Attachment: prelim_schedule.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 11 Jun 2027 09:53:00 -0700
Subject: FW: Exec workshop — arrival windows and contingency legs

Folks — forwarding Kate's ask. Short checklist for ops: can we commit two contingency shuttle slots and one hire-car (on call) for Thu 24, and produce a seat_matrix.pdf that shows primary vs backup legs? Also need:

1) A canary_legs.csv with alternate flights (carrier, flight, depart, arrive, PNR flag) so procurement can see the fallback costs.
2) Policy note on upgrades: who on the Redwood attendee list is allowed premium economy/first? I think execs only — confirm.
3) A shared Drive link with PNR summaries for Globex TravelOps (read-only).

I can take point on the seat matrix and the Drive link — Rishi can you run the canary legs and price buckets? Karthik, can you confirm transport vendor availability and turnaround cost if we need an extra shuttle at short notice?

On urgency: Kate wants final ticketing by EOD Friday (that's 11 Jun). If ops cannot meet that, propose we push ticketing cutoff to Monday 14 Jun and communicate that to Kate with a clear reason.

Thanks — Ben

Cc: Procurement <procurement@globex.com>, TravelOps <travel@globex.com>
Date: Sun, 20 Jun 2027 11:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Exec workshop — arrival windows and contingency legs

Ben — thanks for the quick turnaround and the docs. Confirming the following:

- Globex will designate four names as "guaranteed-window" (they must arrive by 12:30). I'll send that list in a separate email after this thread (security clearance is pending on two VPs).
- Procurement is happy with the shared Drive PNR summary approach; they will request the invoice reconciliation row to reference the canary_legs.csv so we have matching cost buckets.
- TravelOps: please confirm you received seat_matrix.pdf and canary_legs.csv (I see them in the Drive link).

One ask: if one of the guaranteed-window flights is delayed beyond 16:30, can Redwood commit to a dedicated car (not shared shuttle) at our cost? Procurement asked that we avoid putting execs into mixed shuttles after 16:30.

If you can confirm that last item I can clear final ticket purchases today.

Best,
Kate
Head of Executive Programs
Globex Corporation
